::: {#thm-saturated-mle}

#### The saturated model fits each pattern's observed proportion

The maximum likelihood estimate of $\prob_k$ in the [saturated model](#def-saturated-model) is the observed proportion of events among the replicates of pattern $k$:

$$
\hat\prob_k = \frac{\nevents_k}{\nreps_k}.
$$

:::

::: proof
Independence gives each pattern its own log-likelihood term, and the outcomes at pattern $k$ contribute $\nevents_k \ln \prob_k + \paren{\nreps_k - \nevents_k} \ln\paren{1 - \prob_k}$.
The terms share no parameters, so each is maximized on its own.
Setting the derivative with respect to $\prob_k$ to zero gives $\nevents_k / \prob_k - \paren{\nreps_k - \nevents_k} / \paren{1 - \prob_k} = 0$.
Multiplying through by $\prob_k \paren{1 - \prob_k}$ gives $\nevents_k \paren{1 - \prob_k} = \paren{\nreps_k - \nevents_k} \prob_k$.
Expanding gives $\nevents_k - \nevents_k \prob_k = \nreps_k \prob_k - \nevents_k \prob_k$.
Adding $\nevents_k \prob_k$ to both sides gives $\nevents_k = \nreps_k \prob_k$, so $\prob_k = \nevents_k / \nreps_k$.
The log-likelihood term increases to this point and decreases after it, so the point is a maximum.
When $\nevents_k = 0$ the term is $\nreps_k \ln\paren{1 - \prob_k}$, which decreases in $\prob_k$ and so peaks at $\prob_k = 0$.
When $\nevents_k = \nreps_k$ the term is $\nreps_k \ln \prob_k$, which peaks at $\prob_k = 1$.
Both agree with $\nevents_k / \nreps_k$.
:::
